items.label: section_header
items.text: WHATMAKESAREACTIONOCCUR?

items.label: text
items.text: Perhaps one of the most important questions to ask in chemistry is'Will a reaction occur?

items.label: text
items.text: We know that,once started, some chemical reactions simply'go with nofurther, continuoushelpfromus.

items.label: text
items.text: For example, ammonia gas and hydrogen chloride gas react together atroomtemperaturetoformthewhitesolid,ammoniumchloride:

items.label: text
items.text: NH(g) + HCI(g) → NH4Cl(s)

items.label: text
items.text: Magnesium, once ignited, will burn in oxygen to form magnesium oxide:

items.label: formula
items.text: Mg(s) + ½O₂(g) → MgO(s)

items.label: text
items.text: In other reactions,rather than the reactants changing completely into the products,a position of equilibrium is reached,with the final mixture containing a measurable amount of both reactants andproducts.

items.label: text
items.text: For example, ethanoic acid dissociates in water In a 0.1 mol dm-3 solutionofethanoicacid,onlyabout1%oftheethanoicacid moleculesarepresentasions:

items.label: text
items.text: CH;COOH(aq) = CH;COO-(aq) + H+(aq)

items.label: text
items.text: Another example is the dimerisation of nitrogen dioxide in the gas phase:

items.label: formula
items.text: 2NO₂(g) ⇌ N₂O₄(g)

items.label: text
items.text: Atatemperatureof298Kandapressureof100kPa,the equilibrium mixture contains about 70% N2O4.

items.label: text
items.text: the reaction has gone to completion.For some other reactions, significant amounts ofboth reactants and products arepresent at equilibrium.Forotherreactions,theequilibriumliessofartothe left that they appear not to take place at all.

items.label: text
items.text: So, perhaps the better question to ask is not'Will a chemical reaction occur?' but'What will be the position of equilibrium? This is thequestionwehopetoanswerin thistopic.
